biodiversity_overview.text: 22,177 GBIF occurrence records for 66 tracked species are attributed to Assam, spanning 1820-2026.
20,724 of these records (93.4%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 20, Mammalia 14, Magnoliopsida 12, Testudines 9, Actinopterygii 5, Squamata 3, Amphibia 2, Liliopsida 1.

threatened_species.text: 11 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
4 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Indian Rhinoceros (VU), Asian Elephant (EN), Tiger (EN), Sloth Bear (VU).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Pied Starling (7,999), Indian Cuckoo (4,351), Indian Spot-billed Duck (1,873), Indian Pond-heron (1,815), Indian White-eye (1,756).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 797 in 2016 to 436 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 4.91% of Assam's area (33 areas intersect the state).
31.8% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (6,599 of 20,724); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Star Tortoise (0.61), Indian Dwarf Banana (0.55), Indian Eyed Turtle (0.55), Carplet (0.55), Narrow-headed Softshell Turtle (0.54).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Assam (equal-weight reference): cell near 25.875N 91.875E (overall rank 10, median rank across weightings 17); cell near 25.875N 92.625E (overall rank 15, median rank across weightings 18); cell near 26.625N 94.125E (overall rank 24, median rank across weightings 39).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 28,697 km2 (36.68% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

3,431.0 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (11.96% of the 2000 extent; 6.12% in 2015-2024, rank 6 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2016 (258.5 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 1.59% of land and population density is 457.3 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
21% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
